title: FOMC minutes — the July 27-28, 2027 meeting (2:00 p.m. ET, three weeks after the decision)
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes), which states the rule verbatim: "The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision." The rule was VERIFIED by this session rather than trusted, by parsing every "(Released <Month> <D>, <YYYY>)" string the page attaches to its own minutes links and differencing each against its meeting's decision day: 45 published pairs, of which 42 sit at EXACTLY D+21 and all 42 land on a Wednesday. The three exceptions are 2023-11-01 -> 2023-11-21 (D+20, Tue), 2024-11-07 -> 2024-11-26 (D+19, Tue) and 2025-12-10 -> 2025-12-30 (D+20, Tue) -- every one a late-year release pulled forward off a holiday week (Thanksgiving, Thanksgiving, New Year). JULY IS TIGHTER THAN THE OVERALL RULE: all six July meetings on the page release at exactly D+21 on a Wednesday, 6 of 6 -- 2021-07-28 -> 2021-08-18, 2022-07-27 -> 2022-08-17, 2023-07-26 -> 2023-08-16, 2024-07-31 -> 2024-08-21, 2025-07-30 -> 2025-08-20, 2026-07-29 -> 2026-08-19 -- because no US market holiday ever falls in a July meeting's D+21 week. 2027-07-28 + 21 days = Wednesday 2027-08-18. The 14:00 ET release time is the standing convention, not separately sourced here. Filed estimate because it is a firm, verified rule applied to a TENTATIVE parent date: the same page states "Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it", so the promotion trigger is the 2027-06-08/09 meeting ratifying July 27-28, after which the Board's own 2027 minutes dates supersede this derivation. Discovered during the fomc-2027-07-28 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: Proposed during the fomc-2027-07-28 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). THIS DEPARTS FROM A SIBLING'S PRECEDENT AND SAYS SO: fomc-2027-06-09 leg 9 observed its own 2027-06-30 minutes date and deliberately did NOT propose it, on the ground that the three-week rule applied to a tentative date is "two inference layers on a self-disclaimed primary". Two things changed since that call, both of them evidence rather than preference. First, the rule is no longer inherited -- this session measured it end-to-end off the page's own release strings and got 42 of 45 at exactly D+21, with a 6-of-6 July sub-rule and a holiday-week explanation covering all three exceptions. Second, the class is already tracked canonically in this calendar: fomc-minutes-2027-06-30 exists as src/domain/market-events/fomc-minutes-2027-06-30.json, proposed by the consumer-confidence-2027-06-29 lane, so declining to propose the July one would leave a hole rather than hold a line. The proposal inherits estimate from its parent and cannot be more confident than its input. IT SITS OUTSIDE THIS EVENT'S +/-5-DAY CORRIDOR, at D+21, and is proposed anyway because a derived date with a measured 6-of-6 rule is exactly the kind of entry the calendar-feeds-itself mechanism exists for; nothing in the parent ledger's stance depends on it. Its own significance for the parent: it is the first Fed communication of substance after the 2027-07-17 -> 2027-07-29 blackout closes, and it lands 28 days before the 2027-09-15 SEP meeting -- inside the 98-day decision-free corridor whose exact midpoint is 2027-07-28. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
